current_activity: division begins its effort to seize Herrlisheim north of Strasbourg; counterattacked by the XXXIX Panzer Corps
notes: Event date: 16 January 1945 (Riviera to the Rhine ch. 28 p. 523: on 16 January the 12th Armored Division began its effort to seize Herrlisheim; p. 526: an ambush at Herrlisheim-Offendorf on 17 January cost the 43d Tank Battalion). Event definition: the division attacks the German Rhine bridgehead at Herrlisheim as part of VI Corps; the date is the opening of the attack, the objective is the town. Relationship: VI Corps unspecified_subordination (from 6 Jan 45 to 2 Feb 45, CMH table); Seventh Army assigned (from 5 Dec 44, CMH table); 6th Army Group assigned (from 5 Dec 44, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. Location: Herrlisheim, Bas-Rhin. Coordinates: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Herrlisheim, Bas-Rhin). Event support: moderate (one Green Book chapter, two pages; the CMH table lists the division with VI Corps from 6 January). Location support: moderate (named objective town).

current_activity: division command post at Colmar; the division is in reserve north of Colmar during the final Colmar Pocket offensive
notes: Event date: 4 February 1945 (CMH ETO-OB lists the 12th Armored Division command post at Colmar, Haut-Rhin, on 4 February; Riviera ch. 29 p. 548 has the division remaining in reserve north of Colmar for the renewed offensive of 1 February). Event definition: the division headquarters is listed in the Colmar area while the Colmar Pocket is being reduced; Riviera p. 548 has XXI Corps (Milburn) to control the American infantry divisions for the final drive on Neuf-Brisach. Relationship: XXI Corps unspecified_subordination (from 3 Feb 45 to 10 Feb 45, CMH table); Seventh Army assigned (from 5 Dec 44, CMH table); 6th Army Group assigned (from 5 Dec 44, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. Location: Colmar (CMH ETO-OB command-post list, R519 p. 527: listed 4 February 1945); the town centre stands for the command post. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Colmar. Event support: moderate (CMH table and one Green Book page agree on the area, not the day). Location support: moderate (command post listed on the date).
